# Spotter assessment handoff

The public archive defaults to a reproducible synthetic trip with 620 modeled miles, 12 gallons purchased, and a purchase cost of $36.00. For an actual driving route, use the authorized data setup below. The synthetic route is for demonstration only.

## Windows setup

Open PowerShell in the extracted project folder. Install Python 3.12 or later and Git only if you plan to publish the source. The demo can run directly from the extracted folder. The commands below use the virtual environment's Python without changing PowerShell's script execution policy.

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip
& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip check
& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py test
```

Replace `-3.12` with the installed version selector if using a newer Python.

### Synthetic mode

In the first PowerShell window, start the local routing fixture.

```powershell
& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scripts.demo_provider
```

In a second PowerShell window opened at the project root, start Django on loopback.

```powershell
Remove-Item Env:PILOT_CSV,Env:PRICE_CSV,Env:OSRM_URL -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000 --noreload --insecure
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/, select **Use demo coordinates**, and click **Calculate Route**. The demo should show the **Synthetic demo** badge. The `--insecure` flag serves static files during local development with `DEBUG=0`. Keep the server on loopback for the demo.

### Authorized real-data mode

Place these two exact files in the ignored `private-data/` directory, using copies you are authorized to use.

| File | Role | SHA-256 of the tested input |
|---|---|---|
| `fuel-prices-for-be-assessment.csv` | Original assessment OPIS prices | `c704371f141ded9c54df6c32d488a0ba2ceb589f88c936c967daa5330e0cd241` |
| `verified_stations.csv` | Prepared station coordinates and provenance. The tested snapshot has 505 verified US stations. | `1354f0c27470c6f49b2702f5f47ea983814d88a78ae67d5bba18bbbddc613d43` |

Neither input is in the ZIP. Those two inputs suffice for the runtime demonstration. The offline rebuild in [README.md](README.md) requires authorized operator feed and page snapshots and the applicable pilot reviews to reproduce the historical catalog. Census and OpenStreetMap evidence are used in the documented preparation workflows. Use the same authorized snapshots for an exact historical rebuild.

**Private evaluator sharing remains conditional.** The supplied OPIS file had no express redistribution grant in the material provided. The coordinate catalog combines OPIS-linked records with operator-derived data. The reviewed Love's and TA site terms restrict reuse or distribution. An evaluator who already has the authorized OPIS export can use their own copy. Before sending either restricted file privately, obtain written permission or confirm that an existing license expressly covers the evaluator, files, and intended assessment use. A private link alone does not establish redistribution rights. [Love's terms](https://www.loves.com/terms-of-use) · [TA terms](https://www.ta-petro.com/terms-conditions-web/)

Stop the synthetic Django server before switching. The synthetic provider is unnecessary in real-data mode.

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\private-data | Out-Null
# Place the authorized files in private-data before running the following commands.
Get-FileHash .\private-data\fuel-prices-for-be-assessment.csv -Algorithm SHA256
Get-FileHash .\private-data\verified_stations.csv -Algorithm SHA256
$env:PILOT_CSV = (Resolve-Path .\private-data\verified_stations.csv).Path
$env:PRICE_CSV = (Resolve-Path .\private-data\fuel-prices-for-be-assessment.csv).Path
$env:OSRM_URL = 'https://router.project-osrm.org'
$env:SPOTTER_LOG_PROVIDER_REQUESTS = '1'
& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000 --noreload --insecure
```

The page should show **Authorized real data**. OSRM is a shared demo provider. Census is called for street addresses, and OpenStreetMap tiles are used for the basemap when reachable.

## Real-route request examples

Paste this into a separate PowerShell window while authorized mode is running. It sends the exact audited coordinate pairs to the existing endpoint.

```powershell
$routes = @(
  @{ label='Tulsa to Cincinnati'; start=@{latitude=36.154; longitude=-95.9928}; finish=@{latitude=39.1031; longitude=-84.512} }
  @{ label='Albuquerque to Las Vegas'; start=@{latitude=35.0844; longitude=-106.6504}; finish=@{latitude=36.1699; longitude=-115.1398} }
  @{ label='San Francisco to Salt Lake City'; start=@{latitude=37.7749; longitude=-122.4194}; finish=@{latitude=40.7608; longitude=-111.8910} }
  @{ label='Atlanta to Baton Rouge'; start=@{latitude=33.749; longitude=-84.388}; finish=@{latitude=30.4515; longitude=-91.1871} }
)
foreach ($route in $routes) {
  $body = @{ start=$route.start; finish=$route.finish } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3
  $plan = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/fuel-routes/' -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $body
  [pscustomobject]@{
    Route = $route.label
    BaseMiles = $plan.route_miles
    ModeledMiles = $plan.total_miles_estimate
    Stops = @($plan.fuel_stops).Count
    GallonsPurchased = ($plan.fuel_stops | Measure-Object -Property gallons_purchased -Sum).Sum
    PurchaseCostUSD = $plan.estimated_fuel_purchases_usd
  }
}
```

Observed results from the authorized assessment run. Live provider routes and catalog revisions can change these values.

| Journey | Base miles | With estimated detours | Stops | Gallons purchased | Purchase cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Tulsa to Cincinnati | 743.053 | 743.525 | 1 | 24.3525 | $80.38 |
| Albuquerque to Las Vegas | 571.512 | 571.925 | 1 | 7.1925 | $24.72 |
| San Francisco to Salt Lake City | 736.142 | 736.706 | 2 | 23.6706 | $88.11 |
| Atlanta to Baton Rouge | 526.629 | 527.025 | 1 | 2.7025 | $8.50 |

## Interpretation of total fuel cost

The original requirement says **“Calculate the total estimated fuel expenditure.”** The API returns `estimated_fuel_purchases_usd` for the gallons bought at the selected stops. It starts with 50 gallons and places no dollar value on that starting inventory. A drive within the starting tank's capacity can therefore consume fuel and show $0.00 in additional purchases.

The estimated value of **all fuel consumed** would include the portion of the starting fuel consumed plus the value of fuel purchased and consumed along the way. It would need a starting fuel price and a stated valuation method. The API meets the expenditure requirement if it means purchases during the journey. It does not fully satisfy an interpretation that requires the dollar value of all fuel consumed. The submission should disclose this assumption.

Station detours are geometric estimates, the catalog is partial, and the model permits zero estimated fuel at arrival. These affect interpretation of the live examples. Windows commands are documented. The final test suite was executed on Linux.

# Five-minute Loom script

Start `python -m scripts.demo_provider` in one terminal. In another, run `python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000 --noreload --insecure`. On Windows, use the [PowerShell quickstart](../README.md#run-the-synthetic-demo). Open the planner at http://127.0.0.1:8000/. Keep the recording in synthetic mode for public sharing.

| Time | Screen and narration |
|---|---|
| 0:00–0:45 | Introduce the planner and show the **Synthetic demo** badge, start and destination fields, and vehicle assumptions. “The planner accepts US addresses in authorized live mode and coordinates in latitude–longitude order. The vehicle starts with a full 50-gallon tank.” |
| 0:45–1:45 | Click **Use demo coordinates**, then **Calculate Route**. Pan or zoom the map and open the fuel stop marker. “The route line is the GeoJSON returned by the API. The marker shows the station name, per-gallon price, and how much to buy.” |
| 1:45–2:35 | Show the trip summary and fuel stops. “This fictional route models 620 miles and purchases 12 gallons for $36.00. Detour mileage is an estimate. The synthetic route is for demonstration only.” |
| 2:35–3:25 | Enter an invalid latitude such as `95, -95.9928` and calculate again to show the error. Restore the demo coordinates and use the browser’s responsive view to show the stacked layout. |
| 3:25–4:20 | Show the existing `POST /api/v1/fuel-routes/` request in Postman. Point out `fuel_routes/serializers.py`, the routing and optimizer services, and the template and static files. “The browser calls the same API as Postman. The backend remains responsible for selecting stations and calculating cost.” |
| 4:20–5:00 | Show the test results and README. Explain where an authorized evaluator configures live data and remind viewers that route and detour estimates depend on that catalog. |

Keep the OpenStreetMap attribution visible while recording the map.

# Rebuild the open-source station catalog

The open-source pipeline uses US Census Geocoder as a locator for numbered street addresses and OpenStreetMap for station coordinates. It uses the supplied Spotter CSV only on your machine. Protected operator feeds and snapshots are unnecessary. The app, route API and optimizer consume the resulting CSV without code changes.

## Windows quick start

Extract the rebuild kit **into the extracted Spotter project root** so the existing `scripts`, `tests`, and `docs` directories merge. The kit includes normalized OpenStreetMap snapshots under `private-data/open-osm`. The snapshots contain no OPIS rows, station-to-OPIS crosswalk, or Census requests. Install the same dependencies as in the project README, place your already-authorized Spotter CSV in `private-data`, and run:

```powershell
$python = '.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe'
$prices = 'private-data/fuel-prices-for-be-assessment.csv'
$snapshots = @(Get-ChildItem .\private-data\open-osm\??.json | Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName })

& $python -m scripts.geocode $prices private-data/open_census_pilot.csv --cache private-data/open-census-cache
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The Census batch failed. Check its output and rerun.' }

& $python -m scripts.open_station_catalog $prices private-data/verified_stations.csv private-data/open_station_audit.csv --osm @snapshots --census-pilot private-data/open_census_pilot.csv
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The catalog rebuild failed.' }

Get-FileHash .\private-data\verified_stations.csv -Algorithm SHA256
$env:PILOT_CSV = (Resolve-Path .\private-data\verified_stations.csv).Path
$env:PRICE_CSV = (Resolve-Path $prices).Path
$env:OSRM_URL = 'https://router.project-osrm.org'
& $python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000 --noreload --insecure
```

Use `curl.exe` on PATH for the Census batch; modern Windows includes it. The script invokes `curl` as an executable. Run `manage.py test` in the same virtual environment. The original synthetic setup still works when both CSV environment variables are cleared. If Census is unavailable, omit `--census-pilot` to build from OSM evidence alone; that run may have slightly lower coverage.

## Source and matching rules

1. The numbered-street heuristic finds four suitable street-format inputs in the supplied CSV. Submit them in one official Census multipart batch using `Public_AR_Current`. The script retains empty ZIP columns and caches the response. Two Census responses were `Exact` address-range matches. An address-range match is only a lead. It contributes to verification when a matching OSM fuel feature is within 0.25 miles and meets the locality checks. Use the OSM feature's coordinate.
2. The OSM extraction reads local Geofabrik PBFs. It indexes `amenity=fuel` nodes and closed fuel ways, place nodes, and `highway=motorway_junction` references linked to interstate refs on connected motorway ways. Closed fuel ways use a representative point inside the mapped footprint. The tool does not infer coordinates from exits or locality centers.
3. Verification requires a matching operator or facility label and corroborating locality. Locality comes from the OSM address city or a like-named OSM locality within ten miles. Evidence must also include a linked interstate and exit within 1.5 miles, a corresponding store number, a matching numbered street address, or Census corroboration. When the price row has an interstate and exit, a matching linked exit is required. Conflicting explicit store numbers, explicitly private fuel features, multiple distinct results at the strongest evidence level, and the same OSM feature claimed by multiple OPIS IDs are rejected.
4. The compatible output includes OSM feature URLs and PBF fingerprints. The price file is never submitted to an OSM provider. The pipeline makes no public Nominatim requests.

To regenerate a normalized extract, install `requirements-osm.txt`, download the state PBF and checksum from Geofabrik, verify its checksum, then run:

```powershell
& $python -m pip install -r requirements-osm.txt
& $python -m scripts.open_station_sources private-data/open-osm/NM.json --pbf NM private-data/new-mexico-latest.osm.pbf
```

The bundled JSON is the pinned normalized source for this assessment run. It records the SHA-256 of the PBF it came from. New Geofabrik extracts or Census benchmarks can change results. [Census API](https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/Geocoding_Services_API.html) · [Geofabrik US extracts](https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us.html) · [OSM fuel tagging](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:amenity%3Dfuel) · [OSM exit tagging](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:highway%3Dmotorway_junction)

## Licensing and evaluator handoff

The bundled normalized OSM snapshots are © OpenStreetMap contributors and distributed under the Open Database License 1.0. Keep the attribution and license with copies. Follow the applicable ODbL share-alike and access requirements for downstream databases and public use. Census geocoder data is U.S. Census Bureau data. The kit does not include the submitted addresses or Census output records. [OpenStreetMap attribution and license](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright) · [ODbL 1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/)

The open-source snapshots and scripts can be handed off separately from the supplied CSV. A reviewer who already has authorized access to the Spotter CSV can generate the OPIS-linked catalog locally. The combined `verified_stations.csv` and row-level audit contain OPIS-linked data. The supplied CSV had no express redistribution grant in the materials provided. Confirm applicable OPIS rights and ODbL obligations before distributing those joined outputs. The rebuild kit does not include them.

# Publish after approval

This public candidate was created in a new local Git repository from a source-file allowlist. The private workspace had no usable Git repository, index, or history to inspect. The public branch contains only its new source-only history and synthetic data. If you later find another copy with restricted files committed, pause publication. Ignore rules do not remove tracked files or rewrite history. Create a new allowlisted repository with fresh history. If a contaminated commit has already reached a remote, coordinate cleanup with the host and rights holders before sharing it again.

Create an empty GitHub repository under your account without importing the private workspace or adding an initial commit. After approval, replace `OWNER` with the GitHub account or organization and run these commands from the public checkout. Commit reviewed changes in that checkout first.

```sh
git status --short
git diff --cached --name-only
git log --all --oneline
git log --all --name-only --format= | sort -u
git remote -v
git remote add origin https://github.com/OWNER/spotter-assessment.git
git push --set-upstream origin main
```

On Windows PowerShell, use `Sort-Object -Unique` in place of `sort -u`. If `origin` is already configured, verify its URL and skip the remote-add command.

The status and staged diff should be empty. Review every path in history before adding the remote. The only CSVs should be `fixtures/synthetic-prices.csv` and `fixtures/synthetic-stations.csv`. Use a new empty remote and pause if its history already contains commits. No push or upload is part of local preparation.

FILE: fuel_routes/serializers.py
================================================================================

import math

from rest_framework import serializers


class Coordinates(serializers.Serializer):
    latitude = serializers.FloatField(min_value=-90, max_value=90)
    longitude = serializers.FloatField(min_value=-180, max_value=180)

    def to_internal_value(self, data):
        try:
            return super().to_internal_value(data)
        except OverflowError as exc:
            raise serializers.ValidationError("Coordinates are out of range.") from exc

    def validate(self, attrs):
        if not all(math.isfinite(value) for value in attrs.values()):
            raise serializers.ValidationError("Coordinates must be finite.")
        return attrs


class Endpoint(serializers.Field):
    def to_internal_value(self, value):
        if isinstance(value, str) and 0 < len(value.strip()) <= 250:
            return value.strip()
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            fields = Coordinates(data=value)
            fields.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
            return fields.validated_data
        raise serializers.ValidationError("Provide a US street address or a latitude/longitude object.")


class Journey(serializers.Serializer):
    start = Endpoint()
    finish = Endpoint()

================================================================================
FILE: fuel_routes/services/optimizer.py
================================================================================

"""Continuous purchases on a fixed, ordered route with same-point detours."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal

TANK = Decimal(50)
MPG = Decimal(10)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Stop:
    id: str
    mile: Decimal
    detour: Decimal  # one way
    price: Decimal


def optimize(miles, candidates):
    if miles <= TANK * MPG:
        return Decimal(0), []
    stations = sorted(candidates, key=lambda stop: (stop.mile, stop.id))
    points = [Stop("", Decimal(0), Decimal(0), Decimal(0)), *stations,
              Stop("", miles, Decimal(0), Decimal(0))]
    # A label is incoming fuel -> (cost, previous index, previous fuel, purchase).
    labels = [{} for _ in points]
    labels[0][TANK] = (Decimal(0), None, None, Decimal(0))
    for index, origin in enumerate(points[:-1]):
        for target_index in range(index + 1, len(points)):
            target = points[target_index]
            distance = target.mile - origin.mile
            if distance > TANK * MPG:
                break
            consumption = (distance + origin.detour + target.detour) / MPG
            if consumption > TANK:
                continue
            future = labels[target_index]
            for incoming, (cost, *_) in labels[index].items():
                # At a cost-minimizing extreme point, any positive purchase
                # can leave either a full tank or zero fuel at the next stop.
                departures = {max(consumption, incoming)}
                if index:
                    departures.add(TANK)
                for outgoing in sorted(departures):
                    purchase = outgoing - incoming
                    # Skipping a visit with no purchase saves its detour and leaves more fuel.
                    if index and not purchase:
                        continue
                    remaining = outgoing - consumption
                    total = cost + purchase * origin.price
                    if remaining not in future or total < future[remaining][0]:
                        future[remaining] = (total, index, incoming, purchase)
    if not labels[-1]:
        return None
    index = len(points) - 1
    fuel = min(labels[index], key=lambda amount: (labels[index][amount][0], amount))
    total = labels[index][fuel][0]
    legs = []
    while index:
        _, previous, incoming, purchase = labels[index][fuel]
        if previous:
            legs.append((points[previous], purchase))
        index, fuel = previous, incoming
    return total, list(reversed(legs))

"""Provider adapters and indexed station projection."""
from collections import defaultdict
import csv
from decimal import Decimal
from functools import lru_cache
from hashlib import sha256
import json
import logging
import math
from statistics import median
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.cache import cache
import requests
from shapely import Point, STRtree, box
from shapely.geometry import shape

from .optimizer import Stop

MILES_PER_METER = 1 / 1609.344
CENSUS_URL = "https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/locations/onelineaddress"
CORRIDOR = 3
DETOUR_MULTIPLIER = 1.5
SNAP_RADIUS_METERS = 1000
PROVIDER_LOG = logging.getLogger("spotter.providers")


class TripError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code, status, message):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code, self.status = code, status


def provider_json(url, params, handled=()):
    try:
        provider = "census" if url == CENSUS_URL else "osrm"
        PROVIDER_LOG.info("provider_request %s", provider)
        response = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=(3, 12), allow_redirects=False)
        if 300 <= response.status_code < 400:
            raise TripError("provider_error", 502, "Unexpected provider redirect.")
        if response.status_code not in handled:
            response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()
    except requests.Timeout as exc:
        raise TripError("provider_timeout", 504, "Location or routing provider timed out.") from exc
    except (requests.RequestException, ValueError) as exc:
        raise TripError("provider_error", 502, "Location or routing provider failed.") from exc


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def boundaries():
    source = json.loads(settings.STATE_BOUNDARIES_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return STRtree([shape(feature["geometry"]) for feature in source["features"]
                    if int(feature["properties"]["STATE"]) < 60])


def resolve(value):
    if isinstance(value, str):
        key = "census:" + sha256(value.casefold().encode()).hexdigest()
        coordinates = cache.get(key)
        if coordinates is None:
            payload = provider_json(CENSUS_URL, {"address": value, "benchmark": "Public_AR_Current",
                                                 "format": "json"})
            try:
                matches = payload["result"]["addressMatches"]
                if not isinstance(matches, list):
                    raise ValueError("Invalid geocoder matches")
                if len(matches) != 1:
                    raise TripError("address_unresolved", 422,
                                    "Provide an unambiguous US street address or coordinates.")
                location = matches[0]["coordinates"]
                coordinates = (float(location["x"]), float(location["y"]))
                if not valid_coordinates(*coordinates):
                    raise ValueError("Invalid geocoder coordinates")
            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError) as exc:
                raise TripError("provider_error", 502, "Invalid geocoding response.") from exc
            cache.set(key, coordinates, 86400)
    else:
        coordinates = (value["longitude"], value["latitude"])
    if not len(boundaries().query(Point(*coordinates), predicate="intersects")):
        raise TripError("outside_us", 400, "Both endpoints must be in the United States.")
    return coordinates


def valid_coordinates(lon, lat):
    return -180 <= lon <= 180 and -90 <= lat <= 90


def driving_route(start, finish):
    pair = ";".join(f"{lon:.6f},{lat:.6f}" for lon, lat in (start, finish))
    base = settings.OSRM_URL.rstrip("/")
    key = "osrm:" + sha256(f"{base}:{pair}:{SNAP_RADIUS_METERS}".encode()).hexdigest()
    cached = cache.get(key)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached
    payload = provider_json(
        f"{base}/route/v1/driving/{pair}",
        {"overview": "full", "geometries": "geojson",
         "radiuses": f"{SNAP_RADIUS_METERS};{SNAP_RADIUS_METERS}"}, handled=(400,))
    if isinstance(payload, dict) and payload.get("code") in ("NoRoute", "NoSegment"):
        raise TripError("no_driving_route", 422, "No driving route connects the endpoints.")
    try:
        if payload["code"] != "Ok":
            raise ValueError("OSRM non-success code")
        route = payload["routes"][0]
        geometry = route["geometry"]
        distance = float(route["distance"])
        if not (math.isfinite(distance) and distance >= 0 and geometry["type"] == "LineString"
                and len(geometry["coordinates"]) >= 2
                and all(valid_coordinates(x, y) for x, y in geometry["coordinates"])):
            raise ValueError("Invalid route")
    except (KeyError, TypeError, IndexError, ValueError, OverflowError) as exc:
        raise TripError("provider_error", 502, "Invalid routing response.") from exc
    result = geometry, distance * MILES_PER_METER
    cache.set(key, result, 3600)
    return result


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def load_catalog(pilot, prices, pilot_version, prices_version):
    with pilot.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as stream:
        records = {}
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            if row["match_status"] != "verified":
                continue
            key = row["opis_station_id"]
            source = urlsplit(row["source"])
            if (key in records or not key or not (row["station_name"] or "").strip()
                    or source.scheme != "https" or not source.hostname):
                raise ValueError("Invalid station identity or provenance")
            records[key] = row
    amounts = defaultdict(set)
    with prices.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            key = row["OPIS Truckstop ID"]
            if key in records:
                amount = Decimal(row["Retail Price"])
                if not amount.is_finite() or amount <= 0:
                    raise ValueError("Invalid station price")
                amounts[key].add(amount)
    for key, record in records.items():
        record["latitude"] = float(record["latitude"])
        record["longitude"] = float(record["longitude"])
        if not valid_coordinates(record["longitude"], record["latitude"]):
            raise ValueError("Invalid station coordinate")
        record["price"] = median(sorted(amounts[key]))
    rows = list(records.values())
    return rows, STRtree([Point(row["longitude"], row["latitude"]) for row in rows])


def catalog():
    pilot, prices = settings.PILOT_CSV, settings.PRICE_CSV
    try:
        return load_catalog(pilot, prices, pilot.stat().st_mtime_ns, prices.stat().st_mtime_ns)
    except (OSError, ValueError, ArithmeticError, KeyError, TypeError, csv.Error) as exc:
        raise TripError("catalog_unavailable", 503, "Verified station catalog is unavailable.") from exc


def candidates(geometry, miles, rows, index):
    coordinates = geometry["coordinates"]
    progressed = 0.0
    projections = {}
    for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in zip(coordinates, coordinates[1:]):
        # Local equirectangular projection is adequate for short OSRM segments.
        xscale = 69.093 * max(math.cos(math.radians((y1 + y2) / 2)), .01)
        yscale = 69.093
        dx, dy = (x2 - x1) * xscale, (y2 - y1) * yscale
        length = math.hypot(dx, dy)
        if not length:
            continue
        padx, pady = CORRIDOR / xscale, CORRIDOR / yscale
        for station_index in index.query(box(min(x1, x2) - padx, min(y1, y2) - pady,
                                             max(x1, x2) + padx, max(y1, y2) + pady)):
            row = rows[station_index]
            px, py = (row["longitude"] - x1) * xscale, (row["latitude"] - y1) * yscale
            fraction = min(1, max(0, (px * dx + py * dy) / length**2))
            offset = math.hypot(px - fraction * dx, py - fraction * dy)
            if offset <= CORRIDOR and (station_index not in projections or
                                       offset < projections[station_index][0]):
                projections[station_index] = offset, progressed + fraction * length
        progressed += length
    if not progressed:
        return []
    return [Stop(rows[i]["opis_station_id"], Decimal(str(min(miles, at / progressed * miles))),
                 Decimal(str(offset * DETOUR_MULTIPLIER)), rows[i]["price"])
            for i, (offset, at) in projections.items()]

"use strict";

const element = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
const form = element("route-form");
const startInput = element("start");
const finishInput = element("finish");
const calculate = element("calculate");
const demo = element("load-demo");
const routeError = element("route-error");
const mapError = element("map-error");
const stopList = element("stops-list");
const stopsEmpty = element("stops-empty");
const mapStatus = element("map-status");

const number = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { maximumFractionDigits: 4 });
const currency = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD" });
const unitPrice = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
  style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 4,
});
const metricIds = ["route-miles", "total-miles", "fuel-purchased", "fuel-cost"];
const fieldNames = { start: "Start", finish: "Destination" };

const map = initializeMap();
const routeLayer = map ? L.featureGroup().addTo(map) : null;

function initializeMap() {
  if (!window.L) {
    showMapError("The map could not load. You can still calculate a trip and view its fuel plan.");
    return null;
  }
  const instance = L.map("route-map", {
    scrollWheelZoom: false,
    zoomSnap: 0.5,
  }).fitBounds([[25, -124], [49, -67]]);
  const outlinePane = instance.createPane("state-outlines");
  outlinePane.style.zIndex = "250";
  const tiles = L.tileLayer("https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", {
    maxZoom: 19,
    attribution: '&copy; <a href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright">OpenStreetMap</a> contributors',
  });
  tiles.once("tileerror", () => loadStateOutlines(instance, tiles));
  tiles.addTo(instance);
  L.control.scale({ imperial: true, metric: false }).addTo(instance);
  return instance;
}

async function loadStateOutlines(instance, tiles) {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(element("route-map").dataset.outlinesUrl);
    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error("State outlines unavailable");
    }
    const geometry = await response.json();
    L.geoJSON(geometry, {
      pane: "state-outlines",
      interactive: false,
      attribution: "US Census Bureau",
      style: { color: "#a7b8aa", weight: 1.2, fillColor: "#f4f3e7", fillOpacity: 1 },
    }).addTo(instance);
    const credit = tiles.getAttribution();
    instance.removeLayer(tiles);
    instance.attributionControl.addAttribution(credit);
    showMapError("Basemap unavailable. Showing US state outlines.");
  } catch {
    showMapError("Basemap unavailable. Route and fuel stop overlays can still display.");
  }
}

function showMapError(message) {
  mapError.textContent = message;
  mapError.hidden = false;
}

function parseEndpoint(input) {
  const label = fieldNames[input.name];
  const value = input.value.trim();
  if (!value) {
    throw new Error(`Enter a US street address or coordinates for ${label.toLowerCase()}.`);
  }

  const parts = value.split(",").map((part) => part.trim());
  const decimal = /^[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)$/;
  if (parts.length === 2 && parts.every((part) => decimal.test(part))) {
    const [latitude, longitude] = parts.map(Number);
    if (Math.abs(latitude) > 90 || Math.abs(longitude) > 180) {
      throw new Error(`${label} coordinates are out of range. Use latitude (−90 to 90), longitude (−180 to 180).`);
    }
    return { latitude, longitude };
  }
  return value;
}

function showError(message) {
  routeError.textContent = message;
  routeError.hidden = false;
}

function clearError() {
  routeError.hidden = true;
  routeError.textContent = "";
  for (const input of [startInput, finishInput]) {
    input.removeAttribute("aria-invalid");
    input.removeAttribute("aria-describedby");
  }
}

function markInvalid(input) {
  input.setAttribute("aria-invalid", "true");
  input.setAttribute("aria-describedby", "route-error");
}

function setLoading(loading) {
  form.setAttribute("aria-busy", String(loading));
  calculate.disabled = loading;
  demo.disabled = loading;
  calculate.querySelector(".spinner").hidden = !loading;
  element("calculate-label").textContent = loading ? "Calculating route…" : "Calculate Route";
}

function clearPlan() {
  for (const id of metricIds) {
    element(id).textContent = "—";
  }
  routeLayer?.clearLayers();
  stopList.replaceChildren();
  stopList.hidden = true;
  stopsEmpty.textContent = "Calculate a route to see your fuel plan.";
  stopsEmpty.hidden = false;
  mapStatus.textContent = "Awaiting route";
}

function messageFrom(value) {
  if (typeof value === "string") {
    return value;
  }
  if (value && typeof value === "object") {
    return Object.values(value).map(messageFrom).filter(Boolean).join(" ");
  }
  return "";
}

function responseError(response, data) {
  if (typeof data?.detail === "string") {
    return data.detail;
  }
  for (const input of [startInput, finishInput]) {
    if (data?.[input.name]) {
      markInvalid(input);
    }
  }
  const fields = Object.entries(fieldNames)
    .filter(([key]) => data?.[key])
    .map(([key, label]) => `${label}: ${messageFrom(data[key])}`);
  return fields.join(" ") || `The request failed (HTTP ${response.status}). Please try again.`;
}

function stopDetails(stop) {
  const name = document.createElement("strong");
  name.textContent = stop.station_name;
  const purchase = document.createElement("p");
  purchase.textContent = `${unitPrice.format(stop.price_per_gallon_usd)} / gal · Buy ${number.format(stop.gallons_purchased)} gal`;
  return [name, purchase];
}

function renderPlan(plan) {
  const totalGallons = plan.fuel_stops.reduce(
    (sum, stop) => sum + Number(stop.gallons_purchased), 0,
  );
  element("route-miles").textContent = number.format(plan.route_miles);
  element("total-miles").textContent = number.format(plan.total_miles_estimate);
  element("fuel-purchased").textContent = number.format(totalGallons);
  element("fuel-cost").textContent = currency.format(plan.estimated_fuel_purchases_usd);
  element("vehicle-range").textContent = number.format(plan.tank_gallons * plan.miles_per_gallon);
  element("tank-gallons").textContent = number.format(plan.tank_gallons);
  element("initial-gallons").textContent = number.format(plan.initial_gallons);
  element("efficiency").textContent = number.format(plan.miles_per_gallon);

  const synthetic = plan.catalog_mode === "synthetic";
  const mode = element("data-mode");
  mode.dataset.mode = plan.catalog_mode;
  mode.textContent = synthetic ? "Synthetic demo" : "Authorized real data";
  element("mode-note").textContent = synthetic
    ? "Synthetic route for demonstration only. Never use for navigation."
    : "Authorized station data. Detour mileage is estimated.";

  for (const stop of plan.fuel_stops) {
    const item = document.createElement("li");
    item.append(...stopDetails(stop));
    stopList.append(item);
  }
  stopList.hidden = plan.fuel_stops.length === 0;
  stopsEmpty.hidden = plan.fuel_stops.length > 0;
  stopsEmpty.textContent = "No fuel purchases are needed for this route.";
  const count = plan.fuel_stops.length;
  mapStatus.textContent = `${count} fuel ${count === 1 ? "stop" : "stops"} planned`;

  if (routeLayer) {
    renderMap(plan);
  }
}

function renderMap(plan) {
  L.geoJSON(plan.geometry, {
    style: { color: "#196e53", weight: 6, opacity: 0.93 },
  }).addTo(routeLayer);

  plan.fuel_stops.forEach((stop, index) => {
    const popup = document.createElement("div");
    popup.append(...stopDetails(stop));
    L.marker([stop.latitude, stop.longitude], {
      icon: L.divIcon({
        className: "fuel-marker",
        html: String(index + 1),
        iconSize: [28, 28],
        iconAnchor: [14, 14],
      }),
      alt: stop.station_name,
      title: stop.station_name,
    }).bindPopup(popup).addTo(routeLayer);
  });
  const bounds = routeLayer.getBounds();
  if (bounds.isValid()) {
    map.fitBounds(bounds, { padding: [26, 26], maxZoom: 12 });
  }
}

demo.addEventListener("click", () => {
  startInput.value = "36.154, -95.9928";
  finishInput.value = "39.1031, -84.512";
  clearError();
});

form.addEventListener("submit", async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  if (calculate.disabled) {
    return;
  }
  clearError();
  clearPlan();

  const payload = {};
  for (const input of [startInput, finishInput]) {
    try {
      payload[input.name] = parseEndpoint(input);
    } catch (error) {
      markInvalid(input);
      showError(error.message);
      input.focus();
      return;
    }
  }

  setLoading(true);
  mapStatus.textContent = "Calculating…";
  try {
    const response = await fetch(form.action, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", Accept: "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
    });
    const data = await response.json().catch(() => null);
    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(responseError(response, data));
    }
    if (!data?.geometry || !Array.isArray(data.fuel_stops)) {
      throw new Error("The server returned an incomplete fuel plan. Please try again.");
    }
    renderPlan(data);
  } catch (error) {
    clearPlan();
    mapStatus.textContent = "Route unavailable";
    showError(error instanceof TypeError
      ? "The planner could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again."
      : error.message);
  } finally {
    setLoading(false);
  }
});

from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.exceptions import RequestDataTooBig
from django.shortcuts import render
from django.views.decorators.http import require_safe
from rest_framework.decorators import api_view
from rest_framework.response import Response

from .serializers import Journey
from .services.optimizer import MPG, TANK, optimize
from .services.routing import TripError, candidates, catalog, driving_route, resolve


@require_safe
def route_planner(request):
    return render(request, "fuel_routes/planner.html", {
        "synthetic_catalog": settings.SYNTHETIC_CATALOG,
        "tank_gallons": int(TANK),
        "initial_gallons": int(TANK),
        "miles_per_gallon": int(MPG),
        "vehicle_range": int(TANK * MPG),
    })


@api_view(["POST"])
def fuel_route(request):
    try:
        # Let Django check the body size before DRF reads the JSON stream.
        request.body
    except RequestDataTooBig:
        return Response({"code": "request_too_large", "detail": "Request body exceeds 4096 bytes."},
                        status=413)
    query = Journey(data=request.data)
    query.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
    try:
        start = resolve(query.validated_data["start"])
        finish = resolve(query.validated_data["finish"])
        geometry, miles = driving_route(start, finish)
        rows, index = catalog()
        nearby = candidates(geometry, miles, rows, index) if miles > TANK * MPG else []
        result = optimize(Decimal(str(miles)), nearby)
        if result is None:
            raise TripError("no_feasible_fuel_plan", 422,
                            "No feasible fueling plan with the available verified stations.")
    except TripError as exc:
        return Response({"code": exc.code, "detail": str(exc)}, status=exc.status)
    cost, plan = result
    records = {row["opis_station_id"]: row for row in rows}
    stops = []
    for station, gallons in plan:
        row = records[station.id]
        stops.append({
            "opis_station_id": station.id,
            "station_name": row["station_name"],
            "latitude": row["latitude"],
            "longitude": row["longitude"],
            "source": row["source"],
            "route_mile": round(station.mile, 3),
            "round_trip_detour_miles_estimate": round(2 * station.detour, 3),
            "gallons_purchased": round(gallons, 4),
            "price_per_gallon_usd": str(station.price),
        })
    detours = sum((2 * stop.detour for stop, _ in plan), Decimal(0))
    return Response({
        "geometry": geometry,
        "route_miles": round(miles, 3),
        "total_miles_estimate": round(Decimal(str(miles)) + detours, 3),
        "estimated_fuel_purchases_usd": str(cost.quantize(Decimal(".01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)),
        "tank_gallons": int(TANK),
        "initial_gallons": int(TANK),
        "miles_per_gallon": int(MPG),
        "catalog_verified_stations": len(rows),
        "catalog_mode": "synthetic" if settings.SYNTHETIC_CATALOG else "configured",
        "detour_model": "estimated_out_and_back",
        "detour_road_verified": False,
        "fuel_stops": stops,
    })

# Spotter fuel route assessment

A Django REST API that plans partial fuel purchases along one driving route. The vehicle starts with a full 50-gallon tank, has a 500-mile maximum range at 10 MPG, and has no mandatory arrival reserve. The reported cost covers purchases during the journey.

## Fresh-clone setup

Use Python 3.12 or newer on Windows, Linux, or macOS. Django 6.1.3 and Django REST Framework 3.18.3 are pinned in `requirements.txt`. The tests use generated or bundled synthetic fixtures and mock the network.

```sh
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip check
python manage.py check
python manage.py test
```

On Windows, run the equivalent commands in PowerShell from the repository root. Calling the virtual environment's Python directly also works when script activation is restricted.

```powershell
py -3 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip check
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py check
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py test
```

### Run the synthetic demo

In one terminal, run `python -m scripts.demo_provider`. It listens on loopback port 8767 and serves one fictional route. In a second terminal, start Django using the same virtual environment. Use the PowerShell commands on Windows.

```sh
SPOTTER_LOG_PROVIDER_REQUESTS=1 python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000 --noreload --insecure
```

On Windows, start the provider in the first terminal with `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scripts.demo_provider`. Start Django in the second terminal with the following commands.

```powershell
$env:SPOTTER_LOG_PROVIDER_REQUESTS = "1"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000 --noreload --insecure
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8000/**, click **Use demo coordinates**, then click **Calculate Route**. The browser draws the API's GeoJSON and lets you click each station for its price and purchase quantity. Enter street addresses in authorized real-data mode, or enter coordinates in `latitude, longitude` order. The default synthetic provider recognizes only the demo coordinate pair.

The development-only `--insecure` flag serves static assets with the project's default `DEBUG=0`. For deployment, run `python manage.py collectstatic` and serve the collected `staticfiles/` directory with your web server. The repository bundles Leaflet 1.9.4 under its BSD license. Basemap tiles come from OpenStreetMap and require internet access. If tiles are unavailable, the map uses the bundled US Census state outlines and still displays the route overlay and fuel plan. [OpenStreetMap attribution](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright) · [Tile usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/)

To call the API directly, send the fixture request from a third terminal or import `spotter.postman_collection.json`.

```sh
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/fuel-routes/ \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"start":{"latitude":36.154,"longitude":-95.9928},"finish":{"latitude":39.1031,"longitude":-84.512}}'
```

In PowerShell, use **Postman** or `Invoke-RestMethod` to avoid shell quoting differences. Import `spotter.postman_collection.json`, keep `base_url` at `http://127.0.0.1:8000`, and send **Synthetic demo — fuel stop** after both processes start.

Expect HTTP 200, `catalog_mode: synthetic`, a GeoJSON LineString, 620 modeled miles, one fictional stop, 12 gallons, and **$36.00**. The length and station are fixture inputs for illustrating the optimizer. They provide no navigation guidance. The loopback provider has only the documented coordinate pair. The Postman collection includes a repeat request, an invalid request, and separately labeled live examples for authorized real-data mode.

## API and project layout

- `config/` holds Django settings, root URL routing, and WSGI and ASGI entry points.
- `fuel_routes/serializers.py` and `fuel_routes/views.py` validate coordinates or complete US street addresses and format the response. Bare city names should be supplied as coordinates. Census address matching is used in live mode.
- `fuel_routes/services/routing.py` resolves endpoints, calls OSRM once on a typical uncached journey, caches successful routes, validates the station catalog, and uses a spatial index to find near-route stations.
- `fuel_routes/services/optimizer.py` compares fuel purchases along ordered, reachable legs. It accounts for the inbound and outbound portion of estimated station detours and accepts fractional purchases.
- Offline modules in `scripts/` support optional, authorized catalog preparation. They are outside the request path.
- `fuel_routes/templates/` and `fuel_routes/static/` contain the planner page, styles, browser code, and Leaflet assets.
- `tests/` contains the automated suite, `fixtures/` holds the synthetic catalog, and `resources/geo/` holds the state boundaries.

GeoJSON uses longitude–latitude order. Its line and base distance come from the routing provider. Station detours use a geometric out-and-back estimate, with each direction 1.5 times the station’s projected offset. The response keeps detours separate and sets `detour_road_verified` to false. Results depend on the selected route, its candidate stations, and the model. The cache is per process. Concurrent misses may make separate provider calls. Routable points are snapped within 1 km of each endpoint. For a given route, the planner considers verified stations within three geometric miles of the route. It uses the median of distinct OPIS `Retail Price` values by station ID, assuming USD per gallon. The supplied CSV has no observation dates or fuel-grade field, so those prices are assessment inputs.

The estimated purchase cost excludes fuel already in the tank. A trip within the initial modeled range can show $0.00 in purchases while still consuming fuel. The planner can arrive with zero estimated gallons. It works within one provider-selected route and a limited station catalog. Road access, current prices, and a practical fuel reserve require separate verification.

## Authorized real-data evaluation

The uploaded OPIS CSV, operator coordinates, operator snapshots, and previous audit results belong in an authorized private handoff or a directory outside Git. The source checkout contains the code and the fictional dataset. The evaluator needs the OPIS export and permission to use and retain operator snapshots. The original audit found no express public redistribution grant for the supplied price export. Love’s and TA site terms restrict copying or redistributing source material. Obtain clearance before downloading or reusing those sources where required. Keep raw and derived files private. [Love’s terms](https://www.loves.com/terms-of-use) · [TA terms](https://www.ta-petro.com/terms-conditions-web/)

With authorized copies, place the price CSV and any supplied operator feed JSON, TA page HTML, and manual review CSV under `private-data/`. The rebuild uses files on disk. The optional pilot requires `curl` on PATH and uses `filelock` to protect the cache across processes. It calls the US Census batch service for four suitable street records, caches the result by request fingerprint, and leaves unresolved matches out of planning. Add `--reviews private-data/reviews.csv` only if authorized operator evidence is available. [Census geocoding API](https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/Geocoding_Services_API.html)

```sh
mkdir -p private-data
python -m scripts.geocode private-data/fuel-prices-for-be-assessment.csv private-data/pilot.csv \
  --cache private-data/geocode-cache
python -m scripts.station_matching snapshot private-data/operator_snapshot.json \
  --loves private-data/loves-bulk.json \
  --ta https://www.ta-petro.com/location/wa/ta-seattle-east private-data/ta-seattle-east.html \
  --ta https://www.ta-petro.com/location/nv/ta-sparks private-data/ta-sparks.html
python -m scripts.station_matching build private-data/fuel-prices-for-be-assessment.csv private-data/pilot.csv \
  private-data/operator_snapshot.json private-data/verified_stations.csv private-data/pilot_audit.csv
```

The Love’s input is an authorized saved response from its store locator feed at `https://www.loves.com/api/fetch_stores`. TA inputs are saved pages containing station JSON-LD. The TA arguments can be omitted if those snapshots are unavailable. Source files and manual reviews determine the resulting coverage. Reproducing the historical catalog requires the same snapshots and reviews. A provided authorized catalog can also be used directly.

OpenStreetMap extracts are optional review evidence. To prepare them, install `requirements-osm.txt`, download authorized regional Geofabrik PBFs, and run `python -m scripts.osm_extract private-data/osm_evidence.json --pbf NM private-data/new-mexico.osm.pbf`. Pass `--osm private-data/osm_evidence.json` to the build. An OSM proximity candidate by itself never becomes a verified station. The state boundary layer is based on US Census cartographic boundaries. [Geofabrik downloads](https://download.geofabrik.de/) · [OSM attribution and ODbL](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright) · [Census boundary conversion](https://eric.clst.org/tech/usgeojson/)

```sh
export PILOT_CSV="$PWD/private-data/verified_stations.csv"
export PRICE_CSV="$PWD/private-data/fuel-prices-for-be-assessment.csv"
export OSRM_URL=https://router.project-osrm.org
python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000 --insecure
```

Run live smoke journeys separately with `python -m scripts.live_routes`. The public OSRM endpoint is a shared demo service. Use a permitted endpoint for sustained evaluation.

## Local and deployment settings

The default settings are for loopback HTTP and use an ephemeral generated secret. `SPOTTER_LOG_PROVIDER_REQUESTS=1` logs only the provider name. The two catalog paths must be set together to switch to authorized data. `.env.example` documents supported environment variables. Django reads exported variables. In PowerShell, set variables with `$env:NAME = 'value'`. Relative catalog paths are resolved from the repository root. For multiline POSIX examples, use one line in PowerShell or replace each shell continuation with a PowerShell backtick.

| Deployment warning from local settings | HTTPS example in `config/settings_production.py` |
|---|---|
| W002, frame protection | Enables Django frame protection with `DENY`. |
| W003, CSRF middleware | Enables Django CSRF middleware. The current JSON endpoint has no login or cookie-based workflow. Recheck CSRF and auth together before introducing either. |
| W004, HSTS | Sets an initial one-hour policy for a confirmed HTTPS host. |
| W008, HTTPS redirects | Redirects HTTP to HTTPS. Configure trusted proxy TLS signaling only if the proxy strips attacker-supplied forwarding headers and sets its own. |

For an HTTPS deployment, generate a persistent Django secret with `django.core.management.utils.get_random_secret_key()`, store it in the deployment secret store, and inject it as `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY`. Inject the remaining environment values as appropriate for your host.

```sh
export DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=spotter.example.invalid
export PILOT_CSV=/srv/private/verified_stations.csv
export PRICE_CSV=/srv/private/fuel-prices-for-be-assessment.csv
export OSRM_URL=https://routing.example.invalid
python manage.py check --deploy --settings=config.settings_production
```

Replace the example hosts and paths with your actual values. Use these settings only with an HTTPS-capable deployment. Django's two remaining example warnings are W005 and W021. Enable HSTS for subdomains or request preload only after confirming every affected subdomain supports permanent HTTPS and the domain meets browser preload requirements. Public operation would also need access controls, resource limits and data rights. This project is an assessment demo.

"""Loopback-only, deterministic OSRM response for the fictional assessment demo."""
import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

DEMO_ROUTE = "/route/v1/driving/-95.992800,36.154000;-84.512000,39.103100"


class DemoProvider(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        if urlsplit(self.path).path == DEMO_ROUTE:
            status = 200
            body = {
                "code": "Ok",
                "routes": [{"distance": 620 * 1609.344, "geometry": {
                    "type": "LineString",
                    "coordinates": [[-95.9928, 36.154], [-91.5, 38.0], [-84.512, 39.1031]],
                }}],
            }
        else:
            status = 400
            body = {"code": "NoRoute"}
        content = json.dumps(body).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(content)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(content)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8767), DemoProvider) as server:
        server.serve_forever()

"""Deterministic, resumable 100-station geocoding pilot."""
import argparse
from collections import defaultdict
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import math
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
from tempfile import NamedTemporaryFile

from filelock import FileLock

STATES = set("AL AK AZ AR CA CO CT DE DC FL GA HI ID IL IN IA KS KY LA ME MD MA MI MN MS MO MT NE NV NH NJ NM NY NC ND OH OK OR PA RI SC SD TN TX UT VT VA WA WV WI WY".split())
FIELDS = ["opis_station_id", "station_name", "original_address", "city", "state",
          "latitude", "longitude", "source", "match_status", "confidence",
          "address_type", "evidence"]
CENSUS = "https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/locations/addressbatch"


def address_type(address):
    if re.search(r"\bEXIT\b", address, re.I):
        return "highway_exit"
    if re.match(r"^\d+\s+[A-Z]", address, re.I) and not re.search(r"[&/@]|\bCORNER\b", address, re.I):
        return "street"
    return "ambiguous"


def sample(path):
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    seen = set()
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            key = row["OPIS Truckstop ID"]
            if row["State"] in STATES and key not in seen:
                seen.add(key)
                groups[address_type(row["Address"])].append(row)
    selected = []
    for kind, quota in [("street", 4), ("highway_exit", 55), ("ambiguous", 41)]:
        ranked = sorted(groups[kind], key=lambda row: hashlib.sha256(
            ("spotter-pilot-v1:" + row["OPIS Truckstop ID"]).encode()).digest())
        if len(ranked) < quota:
            raise ValueError(f"Insufficient records for {kind}")
        selected.extend(ranked[:quota])
    return selected


def csv_bytes(rows):
    buffer = io.StringIO(newline="")
    csv.writer(buffer).writerows(rows)
    return buffer.getvalue().encode()


def atomic_write(path, payload):
    with NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent, delete=False) as stream:
        staging = Path(stream.name)
        stream.write(payload)
    try:
        staging.replace(path)
    finally:
        staging.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def parse_batch(payload, expected):
    results = {}
    for row in csv.reader(io.StringIO(payload.decode("utf-8-sig"))):
        if len(row) < 3 or row[0] not in expected or row[0] in results:
            raise ValueError("Unexpected Census response record")
        if row[2] == "Match":
            if len(row) < 8:
                raise ValueError("Incomplete Census match")
            lon, lat = map(float, row[5].split(","))
            if not (-180 <= lon <= 180 and -90 <= lat <= 90):
                raise ValueError("Invalid Census coordinate")
        elif row[2] not in {"No_Match", "Tie"}:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown Census status: {row[2]}")
        results[row[0]] = row
    if results.keys() != expected:
        raise ValueError("Census returned an incomplete batch")
    return results


def run(source, output, cache, reviews=None):
    selected = sample(source)
    request = [[row["OPIS Truckstop ID"], row["Address"], row["City"].strip(), row["State"], ""]
               for row in selected if address_type(row["Address"]) == "street"]
    payload = csv_bytes(request)
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(b"Public_AR_Current\0" + payload).hexdigest()[:16]
    submitted = cache / f"{digest}-input.csv"
    saved = cache / f"{digest}-response.csv"
    expected = {row[0] for row in request}
    batch = {}
    failure = None
    try:
        with FileLock(cache / f"{digest}.lock"):
            if saved.exists():
                batch = parse_batch(saved.read_bytes(), expected)
            else:
                atomic_write(submitted, payload)
                response = subprocess.run(
                    ["curl", "--silent", "--show-error", "--fail", "--max-time", "90",
                     "--form", f"addressFile=@{submitted};type=text/csv",
                     "--form", "benchmark=Public_AR_Current", CENSUS],
                    capture_output=True, check=True)
                batch = parse_batch(response.stdout, expected)
                atomic_write(saved, response.stdout)
    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, ValueError) as exc:
        failure = exc.stderr.decode(errors="replace").strip() if isinstance(
            exc, subprocess.CalledProcessError) else str(exc)
    verified = {}
    if reviews:
        with reviews.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as stream:
            for review in csv.DictReader(stream):
                key = review["opis_station_id"]
                if key in verified or key not in {row["OPIS Truckstop ID"] for row in selected}:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid review ID: {key}")
                lat, lon = float(review["latitude"]), float(review["longitude"])
                if not (math.isfinite(lat) and math.isfinite(lon) and
                        -90 <= lat <= 90 and -180 <= lon <= 180 and
                        review["source"].startswith("https://") and review["evidence"].strip()):
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid review evidence: {key}")
                verified[key] = review
    records = []
    for row in selected:
        key = row["OPIS Truckstop ID"]
        kind = address_type(row["Address"])
        record = dict(zip(FIELDS, [key, row["Truckstop Name"], row["Address"],
                                  row["City"], row["State"], "", "", "",
                                  "unresolved", "none", kind, "Manual review required"]))
        if kind == "street":
            record.update(source="US Census Public_AR_Current",
                          evidence="Census request failed" if failure else "Census returned no match")
            match = batch.get(key)
            if match and match[2] == "Match":
                lon, lat = match[5].split(",")
                record.update(latitude=lat, longitude=lon, match_status="matched_unverified",
                              confidence="medium" if match[3] == "Exact" else "low",
                              evidence=f"Census {match[3]} address-range result: {match[4]}")
            elif match and match[2] == "Tie":
                record.update(match_status="uncertain", evidence="Census returned multiple candidates")
        if key in verified:
            record.update({field: verified[key][field] for field in
                           ("latitude", "longitude", "source", "evidence")})
            record.update(match_status="verified", confidence="high")
        records.append(record)
    atomic_write(output, csv_bytes([FIELDS] + [[item[field] for field in FIELDS] for item in records]))
    if failure:
        raise SystemExit(f"Census error: {failure}. CSV saved; rerun to retry.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("source", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--cache", type=Path, default=Path(".geocode-cache"))
    parser.add_argument("--reviews", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    run(args.source, args.output, args.cache, args.reviews)

"""Exercise Django against real routing and measure cold and warm request times."""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import median
from time import perf_counter

import django

os.environ.setdefault("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "config.settings")
django.setup()

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.test.utils import override_settings
from rest_framework.test import APIClient

JOURNEYS = {
    "Tulsa to Cincinnati": ((36.154, -95.9928), (39.1031, -84.512)),
    "Albuquerque to Las Vegas": ((35.0844, -106.6504), (36.1699, -115.1398)),
    "San Francisco to Salt Lake City": ((37.7749, -122.4194), (40.7608, -111.8910)),
    "Atlanta to Baton Rouge": ((33.749, -84.388), (30.4515, -91.1871)),
    "Honolulu to Los Angeles": ((21.3069, -157.8583), (34.0522, -118.2437)),
}


def run(baseline_catalog=None):
    if settings.SYNTHETIC_CATALOG:
        raise SystemExit("Configure authorized PILOT_CSV and PRICE_CSV before live smoke tests.")
    client = APIClient()
    results = []
    with override_settings(ALLOWED_HOSTS=["testserver"]):
        for title, (start, finish) in JOURNEYS.items():
            cache.clear()
            payload = {key: dict(zip(("latitude", "longitude"), point))
                       for key, point in (("start", start), ("finish", finish))}
            durations = []
            for _ in range(6):
                began = perf_counter()
                response = client.post("/api/v1/fuel-routes/", payload, format="json")
                durations.append((perf_counter() - began) * 1000)
                if response.status_code != 200:
                    break
            result = response.json()
            comparison = {}
            if baseline_catalog is not None:
                with override_settings(PILOT_CSV=baseline_catalog):
                    baseline = client.post("/api/v1/fuel-routes/", payload, format="json")
                baseline_result = baseline.json()
                comparison = {
                    "baseline_status": baseline.status_code,
                    "baseline_code": baseline_result.get("code"),
                    "baseline_cost_usd": baseline_result.get("estimated_fuel_purchases_usd"),
                }
            results.append({
                "journey": title, "http_status": response.status_code, "code": result.get("code"),
                "cold_ms": round(durations[0], 1),
                "warm_median_ms": round(median(durations[1:]), 1) if len(durations) > 1 else None,
                "route_miles": result.get("route_miles"),
                "total_miles_estimate": result.get("total_miles_estimate"),
                "catalog_verified_stations": result.get("catalog_verified_stations"),
                "estimated_fuel_purchases_usd": result.get("estimated_fuel_purchases_usd"),
                "fuel_stops": [stop["station_name"] for stop in result.get("fuel_stops", [])],
                **comparison,
            })
    return results


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--baseline", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(run(args.baseline), indent=2))

"""Join the assessor's local price file to Census and OpenStreetMap evidence."""
import argparse
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import csv
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import re

from shapely.geometry import Point

from .geocode import FIELDS, STATES, address_type, atomic_write, csv_bytes
from .station_matching import STATE_CODES, city_key, interchange, normalize, state_shapes

MAX_EXIT_MILES = 1.5
MAX_CITY_MILES = 10
MAX_CENSUS_MILES = 0.25
SAME_SITE_MILES = 0.12
STORE_NUMBER = re.compile(r"#\s*0*(\d+)\b")
GENERIC_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:travel (?:stops?|centers?|centres?|plazas?)|truck stops?|"
    r"convenience stores?|country stores?|service stations?|gas stations?)\b",
    re.I,
)
ALIASES = {
    "travelcentersofamerica": "ta",
    "tapetro": "ta",
    "pilottravelcenters": "pilot",
    "caseysgeneralstore": "caseys",
}


def label(value):
    key = normalize(GENERIC_WORDS.sub("", STORE_NUMBER.sub("", value)))
    return ALIASES.get(key, key)


def miles(x, y, other_x, other_y):
    return 69.093 * math.hypot((x - other_x) * math.cos(math.radians((y + other_y) / 2)),
                              y - other_y)


def store_ref(tags):
    refs = set()
    for key in ("ref", "brand:ref"):
        raw = tags.get(key, "").strip()
        if re.fullmatch(r"#?\d+", raw):
            refs.add(int(raw.lstrip("#")))
    number = STORE_NUMBER.search(tags.get("name", ""))
    if number:
        refs.add(int(number[1]))
    return refs


def street_key(value):
    return normalize(re.sub(
        r"\b(ST|RD|AVE|BLVD|HWY|DR)\.?\b",
        lambda m: {"ST": "street", "RD": "road", "AVE": "avenue", "BLVD": "boulevard",
                   "HWY": "highway", "DR": "drive"}[m[1].upper()], value, flags=re.I,
    ))


class StateIndex:
    def __init__(self, snapshot, shape):
        self.shape = shape
        self.digest = snapshot["sha256"]
        self.by_label = defaultdict(list)
        self.places = defaultdict(list)
        self.exits = defaultdict(list)
        for site in snapshot["fuel"]:
            _, _, lon, lat, tags = site
            if tags.get("access") in {"no", "private"} or not self.shape.covers(Point(lon, lat)):
                continue
            labels = {label(tags[key]) for key in ("name", "brand", "operator") if tags.get(key)}
            for key in labels - {""}:
                self.by_label[key].append(site)
        for name, lon, lat in snapshot["places"]:
            if self.shape.covers(Point(lon, lat)):
                self.places[city_key(name)].append((lon, lat))
        for ref, lon, lat, roads in snapshot["exits"]:
            for road in roads:
                self.exits[road, normalize(ref)].append((lon, lat))


def match(rows, index, census):
    station = rows[0]
    city = city_key(station["City"])
    roads, exits = interchange(station["Address"])
    junctions = [point for road in roads for ref in exits for point in index.exits[road, ref]]
    possible = {}
    for row in rows:
        name = row["Truckstop Name"]
        number = STORE_NUMBER.search(name)
        for site in index.by_label.get(label(name), ()):
            kind, osm_id, lon, lat, tags = site
            if tags.get("addr:state", station["State"]).upper() != station["State"]:
                continue
            if tags.get("addr:city"):
                if city_key(tags["addr:city"]) != city:
                    continue
                city_evidence = "OSM address city"
            elif any(miles(lon, lat, *point) <= MAX_CITY_MILES for point in index.places.get(city, ())):
                city_evidence = "near matching OSM locality"
            else:
                continue
            refs = store_ref(tags)
            if number and refs and refs != {int(number[1])}:
                continue
            near_exit = any(miles(lon, lat, *point) <= MAX_EXIT_MILES for point in junctions)
            if roads and exits and not near_exit:
                continue
            osm_address = f"{tags.get('addr:housenumber', '')} {tags.get('addr:street', '')}"
            if census and miles(lon, lat, *census) <= MAX_CENSUS_MILES:
                score, reason = 4, "Census Exact range corroborated by matching OSM fuel feature"
            elif number and refs == {int(number[1])}:
                score, reason = 3, "operator and store number"
            elif address_type(station["Address"].strip()) == "street" and (
                street_key(osm_address) == street_key(station["Address"])
            ):
                score, reason = 2, "operator and exact OSM street address"
            elif near_exit:
                score, reason = 1, "operator and interstate exit"
            else:
                continue
            rank = (score, kind == "node", bool(tags.get("name")))
            if (kind, osm_id) not in possible or rank > possible[kind, osm_id][0]:
                possible[kind, osm_id] = rank, site, f"{reason}; {city_evidence}"
    if not possible:
        return None, "insufficient_independent_evidence"
    best = max(item[0][0] for item in possible.values())
    finalists = [item for item in possible.values() if item[0][0] == best]
    chosen = max(finalists, key=lambda item: (item[0], -item[1][1]))
    _, (_, _, lon, lat, _), evidence = chosen
    if any(miles(lon, lat, item[1][2], item[1][3]) > SAME_SITE_MILES for item in finalists):
        return None, "multiple_distinct_sites"
    return chosen[1], evidence


def census_matches(pilot):
    if pilot is None:
        return {}
    result = {}
    with pilot.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            if (row["source"] == "US Census Public_AR_Current"
                    and row["evidence"].startswith("Census Exact address-range result:")):
                key = row["opis_station_id"]
                result[key] = (row["original_address"], row["city"], row["state"],
                               float(row["longitude"]), float(row["latitude"]))
    return result


def build(prices, sources, output, audit, pilot=None):
    by_id = defaultdict(list)
    with prices.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            if row["State"] in STATES:
                by_id[row["OPIS Truckstop ID"]].append(row)

    shapes = state_shapes()
    indexes = {}
    for path in sources:
        snapshot = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        state = snapshot["state"]
        if state in indexes or snapshot["license"] != "ODbL-1.0":
            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected or repeated OSM source state: {state}")
        indexes[state] = StateIndex(snapshot, shapes[STATE_CODES[state]])
    candidates = census_matches(pilot)
    claimed = defaultdict(list)
    matches = {}
    reasons = {}
    for key, rows in by_id.items():
        row = rows[0]
        index = indexes.get(row["State"])
        if not index:
            reasons[key] = "extract_not_loaded"
            continue
        census = candidates.get(key)
        if census and (row["Address"], row["City"], row["State"]) != census[:3]:
            census = None
        site, reason = match(rows, index, census[3:] if census else None)
        reasons[key] = reason
        if site:
            claimed[tuple(site[:2])].append(key)
            matches[key] = site

    for keys in claimed.values():
        if len(keys) > 1:
            for key in keys:
                matches.pop(key)
                reasons[key] = "osm_feature_matches_multiple_opis_ids"

    catalog_rows = [FIELDS]
    audit_rows = [["opis_station_id", "state", "outcome"]]
    for key, rows in by_id.items():
        row = rows[0]
        audit_rows.append([key, row["State"], reasons[key]])
        if key not in matches:
            continue
        kind, osm_id, lon, lat, _ = matches[key]
        source = f"https://www.openstreetmap.org/{kind}/{osm_id}"
        evidence = f"{reasons[key]}; ODbL-1.0; OSM extract SHA-256 {indexes[row['State']].digest}"
        catalog_rows.append([key, row["Truckstop Name"], row["Address"], row["City"], row["State"],
                             lat, lon, source, "verified", "high",
                             address_type(row["Address"].strip()), evidence])
    atomic_write(output, csv_bytes(catalog_rows))
    atomic_write(audit, csv_bytes(audit_rows))
    counts = Counter(reasons[key] for key in by_id if key not in matches)
    return {"us_station_ids": len(by_id), "verified": len(matches),
            "unmatched": len(by_id) - len(matches), "unmatched_by_reason": dict(counts),
            "census_exact_candidates": len(candidates),
            "census_corroborated": sum(reasons[key].startswith("Census Exact") for key in matches),
            "states_loaded": sorted(indexes)}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("prices", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("audit", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--osm", type=Path, nargs="+", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--census-pilot", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(build(args.prices, args.osm, args.output, args.audit, args.census_pilot),
                     indent=2, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

FILE: scripts/open_station_sources.py

"""Normalize local OpenStreetMap PBFs into an ODbL source snapshot."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

from .geocode import STATES, atomic_write
from .station_matching import interchange

PLACES = ("city", "town", "village", "hamlet", "suburb", "locality")
TAGS = (
    ("amenity", "fuel"),
    ("highway", "motorway_junction"),
    ("highway", "motorway"),
    ("highway", "motorway_link"),
    *(("place", value) for value in PLACES),
)
FUEL_TAGS = ("name", "brand", "operator", "ref", "brand:ref", "addr:city",
             "addr:state", "addr:housenumber", "addr:street", "access", "hgv")


def extract(path):
    import osmium
    from shapely.geometry import Polygon

    fuel, places = [], []
    exits, roads = {}, {}
    processor = (osmium.FileProcessor(str(path)).with_locations("flex_mem")
                 .with_filter(osmium.filter.TagFilter(*TAGS)))
    for obj in processor:
        tags = obj.tags
        if obj.is_node() and obj.location.valid():
            lon, lat = obj.location.lon, obj.location.lat
            if tags.get("place") in PLACES and tags.get("name"):
                places.append([tags["name"], lon, lat])
            if tags.get("highway") == "motorway_junction" and tags.get("ref"):
                exits[obj.id] = [tags["ref"], lon, lat]
            if tags.get("amenity") == "fuel":
                fuel.append(["node", obj.id, lon, lat,
                             {tag: tags[tag] for tag in FUEL_TAGS if tag in tags}])
        elif obj.is_way():
            if tags.get("highway") in {"motorway", "motorway_link"}:
                refs, _ = interchange(tags.get("ref", ""))
                if refs:
                    for node in obj.nodes:
                        if node.ref in exits:
                            roads.setdefault(node.ref, set()).update(refs)
            if tags.get("amenity") == "fuel" and obj.is_closed() and len(obj.nodes) >= 4:
                if all(node.location.valid() for node in obj.nodes):
                    polygon = Polygon([(node.lon, node.lat) for node in obj.nodes])
                    if polygon.is_valid and polygon.area > 0:
                        point = polygon.representative_point()
                        fuel.append(["way", obj.id, point.x, point.y,
                                     {tag: tags[tag] for tag in FUEL_TAGS if tag in tags}])
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        digest = hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
    return {
        "license": "ODbL-1.0",
        "attribution": "© OpenStreetMap contributors",
        "source": "https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us.html",
        "sha256": digest,
        "fuel": fuel,
        "places": places,
        "exits": [[*entry, sorted(roads[key])] for key, entry in exits.items() if key in roads],
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--pbf", nargs=2, metavar=("STATE", "PATH"), required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    state, path = args.pbf
    if state not in STATES:
        parser.error("Use a two-letter US state code.")
    snapshot = extract(Path(path))
    snapshot["state"] = state
    atomic_write(args.output, json.dumps(snapshot, separators=(",", ":")).encode())
    print(f"{state}: {len(snapshot['fuel'])} fuel features, {len(snapshot['exits'])} linked exits")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()



================================================================================
FILE: scripts/osm_extract.py
